name: Kornephoros
description: A giant of type G7 III 42.7 parsecs away, 15.9 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148856: radius 15.92 +0.41/-0.39 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 3.472 +/- 0.008 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148856: mass 2.91 +/- 0.11 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148856: effective temperature 5092 +/- 64 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148856: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 23.44 +/- 0.58 mas, inverted

text.card: A giant of type G7 III, 43 parsecs away: 15.9 times the Sun's width and 154 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 3.472 milliarcseconds, which gives 15.92 solar radii and 5,092 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 148856: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1297565458994346240 (quality A), from 2004A&A...424..727P; Gaia DR3 measures none
